COUNTERSHAPE EXPERIMENTAL CONTRACT
==================================

This contract reruns one observed behavior from the declared
adapter profile and checks only the listed output fields. It
is a Countershape-generated experimental selected-field
contract.

! WARNING: FULL USER AUTHORITY AND NETWORK ACCESS. This
! executes subject code with your user permissions and host
! network access. It is not a sandbox or containment
! boundary.

CONFIDENTIALITY NOT ESTABLISHED. Exact fixture, input,
environment, and source bytes may be sensitive.

What this contract checks
-------------------------

- Adapter: `CLI`
- Repository-relative subject entrypoint:
  `fixture/subject.mjs`
- Decision action: `ALLOW_OBSERVED`
- Scope: exact witnessed stimulus
  `sha256:40ee16d340e2127e6ce55265e3820cda32da1b9c855fbf8c41
  19735d5281b8d2`
- Selected fields, in order:
  1. `cli.stdout.bytes`

Plain English: the run passes only when the listed fields
match one allowed exact combination from the original
observation. Other context can change without failing this
contract.

Before you run
--------------

Countershape does not prepare the run directory in this
release. Before running the contract, create a source-only
copy of the target.

The prepared target must:

- Contain the repository-relative subject entrypoint shown
  above.
- Contain no `.git` directory, symlink, hardlink, socket,
  device, FIFO, or other special entry.
- Use only supported regular-file modes.
- Remain distinct from and non-nested with the bundle
  directory.

Use an existing reviewed source-export process. If you
cannot make and inspect that copy, stop: this bundle does
not provide a safe preparation command.

This release has been exercised only on local Darwin/arm64
Node. Other platforms may report
`INELIGIBLE_EXECUTION|ENVIRONMENT_INVALID`; a conforming run
does not prove portability.

Run it
------

Run these commands from a shell after preparing the separate
target copy:

    cd "<absolute-prepared-target-root>" &&
    "<absolute-node-executable>" --test \
      --test-reporter=tap \
      "<absolute-bundle-root>/contract.test.mjs"

Replace only the three placeholder texts and leave the
double quotes in place; the shown quoting preserves ordinary
spaces. If a value contains a double quote, dollar sign,
backtick, backslash, or newline, stop and use a reviewed
argv-based launcher instead of editing this shell block.
Direct invocation establishes no Git target identity.

The selected TAP stream contains exactly one machine
diagnostic:

    # COUNTERSHAPE_RESULT_V1|<outcome>|<reason>

Controlled runs keep outer stderr empty. Only
`CONFORMS|NONE` exits zero.

Read the result
---------------

- `CONFORMS|NONE`: the listed behavior matched one allowed
  exact combination.
- `CONTRADICTS|PREDICATE_MISMATCH`: the run was usable, but
  the listed behavior differed.
- `INELIGIBLE_EXECUTION|<reason>`: the run cannot support a
  behavioral conclusion.
- `MALFORMED_CONTRACT`, `TAMPER_DETECTED`, or
  `HARNESS_FAILURE`: artifact, integrity, or control
  failure; do not interpret subject behavior.

If behavior contradicts, inspect the listed fields before
deciding whether the subject or contract should change. For
an ineligible, malformed, tampered, or harness-failure
result, repair the environment or recreate and verify the
bundle through your trusted workflow, then rerun. Those
outcomes are not subject-behavior results.

Integrity and nonclaims
-----------------------

The unchanged contract entrypoint checks every protected
companion file before it imports the harness. A mismatch
with this bundle's expected bytes is reported as an
integrity failure.

Direct invocation does not establish:

- Who created or approved the bundle.
- Authenticity, Git identity, or currentness.
- Correctness or portability beyond this exact run.
- Resistance to coordinated replacement of the bundle.
- Containment or long-term maintainability.
